questions.question: Explain why Venus is too hot and Mars is too cold for life.
questions.expected_answer: Venus is closer to the Sun than the Earth, so it gets much more heat, and its thick clouds trap the heat, so it is hotter than an oven. Mars is further from the Sun than the Earth, so it gets less heat and is very cold, and its water is frozen.

questions.question: Explain why the Earth's distance from the Sun is just right for life.
questions.expected_answer: The Earth is not too close and not too far from the Sun. It gets enough heat and light for plants to make food and for its water to stay liquid, but not so much that the water boils away or living things burn. All living things need liquid water and plants need light, so this distance makes life possible.

questions.question: Give two ways that the Earth's layer of air helps living things.
questions.expected_answer: Any two: it acts like a blanket and keeps the Earth warm at night; it blocks some of the Sun's harmful rays; it contains oxygen that animals and people breathe; it contains the gas plants use to make food.
